data.expected_signal: row quotient overshoots floor(n/7) by 1 for large uint32 values with certain residues mod 7

evidence.summary: Sweep of the last 100000 uint32 values: 14286 of 100000 rows are wrong, all by +1, and all failing inputs have residue n mod 7 = 6. E.g. input 4294867296 gives row 613552471 instead of 613552470. Confirms SHIFT=34 quotient overshoot for residue-6 values near the top of the range, exactly matching the ceil-magic error analysis (5n/(7*2^34) > 6/7 margin).

rationale: With M = ceil(2^34/7) = 2454267027, 7M - 2^34 = 5, so (n*M)>>34 overestimates n/7 by up to 5n/(7*2^34) ≈ 0.1786 at n near 2^32, which exceeds the safety margin; for n with n mod 7 near 6 (frac close to 6/7) the floored quotient overshoots by 1. The ceil-magic method for a uint32 dividend and divisor 7 requires SHIFT ≥ 35.

scope_evidence.summary: 'EVERY unsigned 32-bit value is legal, from 0 through 4294967295 inclusive' and 'Every coordinate must equal the integer mathematical target EXACTLY ... In particular, every col is in [0,6] and 7*row + col equals the original unsigned index in mathematical integers.'
Lines 10-12: _SHIFT = 31 + (7-1).bit_length() = 34; _MULTIPLIER = ceil(2^34/7) = 2454267027; line 21 computes quotient = (value * MULTIPLIER) >> SHIFT.

scope_rationale: The contract explicitly requires exact row=floor(i/7) for every uint32 value including those near 2^32 (e.g., inputs with n mod 7 = 6 and n near 4294967295, which the contract admits since all uint32 values are legal), so an overshooting quotient at these values violates the exactness requirement.
statement: The kernel's reciprocal-multiply quotient (value * 2454267027) >> 34 overshoots floor(n/7) by 1 for some uint32 inputs, e.g. inputs with n mod 7 = 6 near the top of the uint32 range, yielding a row that is one too large.

data.expected_signal: remainder wraps to huge uint32 (e.g. 4294967295) for large indices where quotient overshoots

evidence.summary: Same sweep: 14286 elements have col outside [0,6]; all show col=4294967295 (uint32 wrap of value - 7*overshooting_quotient = -1) with row one too large. The mod-2^32 invariant check passes only because the wrapped col cancels the +1 row error; the mathematical invariant 7*row+col==index with col in [0,6] is violated for all 14286 elements.

rationale: Same overestimate mechanism: when quotient is one too large, 7*quotient exceeds value, so the uint32 cast of value - 7*quotient wraps to a value like 4294967295, breaking the stated invariant that every col lies in [0,6].

scope_evidence.summary: 'every col is in [0,6] and 7*row + col equals the original unsigned index in mathematical integers' — an invariant stated for every legal uint32 index.
Line 22: remainder = value - quotient * 7 (uint64), then .to(tl.uint32) store at line 24 — wraparound if quotient overshoots.

scope_rationale: The contract states the invariant col in [0,6] and 7*row+col == index for every legal uint32 input; a wrapped remainder for any such input directly violates it. This follows from the same in-scope input family (large uint32 values) as the quotient-overshoot claim.
statement: For the same failing inputs, the remainder computed as value - 7*quotient in uint64 then cast to uint32 wraps to a huge value (e.g. 4294967295) instead of a col in [0,6], breaking the invariant 7*row + col == index.

data.expected_signal: if constexpr typing were corrupting the product, even mid-range inputs would show wrong quotients

evidence.summary: On 51000 inputs spanning 0..~1e9 (where SHIFT=34 magic math is provably exact), kernel row and col match the exact int64 reference for every element. No evidence of constexpr MULTIPLIER int32 truncation or 64-bit product corruption; the only failures are the SHIFT=34 range failures already covered by c1/c2.

rationale: Triton constexpr integers can be typed by value; 2454267027 does not fit in int32, so the multiplication or its typing may behave unexpectedly in Triton 3.4, independent of the shift-size analysis.

scope_evidence.summary: 'Every coordinate must equal the integer mathematical target EXACTLY' for every legal uint32 input; any division method is allowed only 'if it satisfies this exact requirement for every legal unsigned index'.
Line 55: _unflatten launched with MULTIPLIER=_MULTIPLIER=2454267027 as a tl.constexpr; line 21 multiplies uint64 value by MULTIPLIER.

scope_rationale: The kernel's exact-quotient computation for any contract-legal input depends on MULTIPLIER being represented at full 64-bit width in the product; a silent int32 truncation would corrupt outputs even for inputs where SHIFT=34 math is otherwise adequate. The contract requires exactness for all uint32 inputs.
statement: The constexpr MULTIPLIER (2454267027 > int32 max) may be typed as a 32-bit signed value in Triton 3.4, causing the 64-bit product value * MULTIPLIER to overflow or sign-extend incorrectly and produce wrong quotients.
